answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by treating reputation as a finite, non-transferable resource. A new identity begins like a small knoll, easily overlooked and possessing no weight. It must prove its unique utility across many epochs; its record builds strength like a persistent zephyr, steady and unmistakable, ensuring no single malicious actor can spawn thousands of voices cheaply. Only when a node proves its history—anchored on the ridge of reliable consensus—does it gain voting power. This keeps the economy decentralized rather than flooded by low-effort, mass-generated accounts.
